name: Malicious LiteLLM PyPI releases 1.82.7 and 1.82.8
summary: The LiteLLM package was compromised and malicious PyPI versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were published with secret-exfiltration behavior.

name: LiteLLM MCP OAuth2 Passthrough Authentication Bypass
summary: A fallback in LiteLLM MCP authentication could allow requests with an arbitrary Bearer token to reach configured MCP tooling without a valid LiteLLM key.

name: LiteLLM MCP Proxy Improper Authentication
summary: LiteLLM MCP proxy authentication logic was affected by improper authentication and fixed in 1.84.0.

name: LiteLLM Custom Code Guardrails Production Safety-Check Bypass
summary: Production create/update paths for custom-code guardrails did not apply the same sandboxing and validation as the test path, enabling code execution under specified privilege conditions.

name: Trivy Ecosystem Supply-Chain Compromise
affected: compromised Trivy release/action ecosystem during incident window
summary: A compromised credential was used to publish malicious Trivy ecosystem artifacts and mutable action references during the March 2026 incident.

name: Trivy Crafted OCI Artifact Path Traversal
summary: A crafted OCI artifact title could cause Trivy to write downloaded layer content outside the intended destination when fetching attacker-controlled artifacts.

name: Semantic Kernel In-Memory Vector Store filter injection to RCE
summary: Prompt injection could reach unsafe string interpolation in Python lambda filters executed via eval(), turning a data lookup into code execution. Microsoft did not publish a CVSS score in the cited post.

name: Semantic Kernel SessionsPythonPlugin arbitrary file access
summary: A helper (DownloadFileAsync) was exposed to the model with unvalidated path parameters, allowing model-controlled file read/write outside the intended sandbox.

name: MCP STDIO configuration command injection across AI frameworks
summary: OX Security reports that unsanitized STDIO server parameters let attacker-influenced MCP configuration execute OS commands across SDK-derived products. Several vendors disputed the finding as intended behaviour of the transport; only identifiers corroborated by more than one source are listed here.

name: LiteLLM proxy command injection in two endpoints
summary: Two LiteLLM proxy endpoints passed caller input to an OS command, giving command execution on the AI gateway host; fixed in 1.83.7. In CISA KEV since 2026-06-08.

name: LiteLLM proxy SQL injection via authorization header
summary: A database query in the LiteLLM proxy was built from the authorization header, allowing SQL injection against the gateway's key store; fixed in 1.83.7. In CISA KEV since 2026-05-08.

name: mcp-remote OS command injection from a malicious MCP server
summary: mcp-remote passed a crafted authorization_endpoint value returned by an untrusted MCP server to the operating system, so connecting to a malicious server could run commands on the client. Fixed in 0.1.16.

name: Flowise CustomMCP remote code execution
summary: Flowise 3.0.5 evaluated user-supplied CustomMCP configuration as code, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution on the LLM-flow server.

name: Claude Code code execution before the startup trust dialog
summary: A bug in Claude Code's startup trust dialog let a malicious project run code before the user accepted the trust prompt; fixed in 1.0.111.

name: Flowise Custom MCP OS command execution without authentication
summary: Flowise's Custom MCP feature, designed to launch local MCP servers with commands such as npx, could be reached without authentication, giving OS command execution (NVD gives versions before 3.0.1; the GitHub advisory lists 3.0.5 as last affected).

name: MLflow path traversal
summary: A path traversal in MLflow before 2.2.1 allowed reading files outside the artifact store on the ML tracking server.

name: Microsoft 365 Copilot AI command injection (information disclosure)
summary: Microsoft describes AI command injection in Microsoft 365 Copilot that let an unauthorized attacker disclose information over a network; fixed by Microsoft in the service.

name: GitHub Copilot and Visual Studio command injection
summary: Improper neutralization in GitHub Copilot and Visual Studio 2022 allowed command injection and local code execution; fixed in Visual Studio 17.14.12.

name: Claude Code project-load flow credential exfiltration
summary: Claude Code's project-load flow let a malicious repository exfiltrate data, including API credentials, before the user trusted the project; fixed in 2.0.65.

name: EmailGPT direct prompt injection
summary: The EmailGPT service let a user inject a direct prompt that took over the service logic and could expose system instructions.

name: Flowise 1.8.2 authentication bypass
summary: Flowise 1.8.2 allowed a remote, unauthenticated attacker to reach API endpoints as an administrator.

name: MCP Inspector unauthenticated proxy remote code execution
summary: MCP Inspector below 0.14.1 had no authentication between the browser client and its local proxy, so a web page could make it launch commands; fixed in 0.14.1.

name: Ray log API local file inclusion
summary: Ray's log API endpoint let unauthenticated callers read any file on the server; the issue is fixed in 2.8.1.

name: mcp-server-git path traversal in git_init
summary: The reference MCP git server accepted arbitrary filesystem paths in git_init, letting a model-issued tool call create repositories outside the intended directory.

name: mcp-server-git argument injection in git_diff and git_checkout
summary: mcp-server-git passed user-controlled arguments from git_diff and git_checkout straight to the git CLI, so a tool call could inject git options.

name: Cursor MCP configuration persistent code execution
summary: Cursor 1.2.4 and below trusted a previously approved MCP configuration after it was modified, giving attackers persistent code execution through a shared repository; fixed in 1.3.

name: nginx-ui MCP integration exposed without authentication
summary: The MCP integration in nginx-ui 2.3.5 and earlier exposed management tools without authentication, letting a client drive the web server's configuration.

name: ChuanhuChatGPT stored cross-site scripting
summary: ChuanhuChatGPT did not sanitize chat content before rendering it, allowing stored cross-site scripting in the LLM chat interface.

name: Zen MCP Server path traversal
summary: Zen MCP Server (PAL MCP Server) before 9.8.2 let authenticated callers read arbitrary files through a path traversal in its tool inputs.

name: CrewAI JSON loader arbitrary local file read
summary: CrewAI's JSON loader tool read files without path validation, so an agent could be steered into reading files on the host.

name: CrewAI RAG tool server-side request forgery
summary: CrewAI's RAG search tools fetched URLs without restriction, enabling server-side request forgery against internal and cloud metadata services.
